SOM.note: No central bank role is stated.
Only a programme grievance system and fraud hotline; no rules for digital financial services.
Disability is mentioned only as youth beneficiaries; nothing on accessible information or digital services.
A phone helpline and centre-based grievance system are described with no web, app, messaging or email channel and no case numbers.

facts.fact: The Baxnaano programme page says MoLSA will pay 50,000 households USD 240 in a single payment in 2025, then USD 60 quarterly in 2026-2027, by mobile money to the phone number registered at enrolment.

systems.owner: Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs

SOM.note: Nothing on local government offices or their connection.
No survey of account ownership is given.

facts.fact: The Baxnaano page tells beneficiaries to keep an active mobile wallet and registered number to receive cash transfers through mobile money.

The page says households for the Baxnaano UCT are identified from the Unified Social Registry by an automated proxy means test, and each selected household is given a Social Registry Number used at enrolment.
The Baxnaano page says all UCT payments are sent by mobile money to the household's registered phone number.
The page says beneficiaries are identified through the Unified Social Registry, a national database of socio-economic data on vulnerable households used to assess eligibility for social support.
